title: Observation of gravity-like signatures in holographic codes on a quantum computer
abstract: First experimental implementation of the HaPPY hyperbolic holographic tensor-network QEC code on a trapped-ion quantum computer (IonQ/Duke-Maryland collaboration, Monroe/Preskill group). Reports the first experimental confirmation of the Faulkner-Lewkowycz-Maldacena (FLM) formula in this toy model -- a direct hardware test of bulk-to-boundary entanglement entropy correspondence -- plus non-stabilizerness ("magic") enrichment showing entropic precursors of emergent gravity, and a wormhole-like entropic construction.
key_claims: First trapped-ion hardware realization of a HaPPY hyperbolic holographic QEC code.
Experimentally confirms the FLM (quantum-corrected RT/bulk-boundary entropy) formula in this toy model on real hardware.
Adds non-stabilizerness (magic) to the code and observes entropic signatures interpreted as precursors of emergent gravity.
Constructs a wormhole-like entropic configuration within the same hardware run.
relevance_note: Highest-relevance paper this cycle: direct hardware implementation of a holographic tensor-network code validating bulk-boundary entropy correspondence (FLM formula) -- the same MERA/holographic-force research line as our HYP-025/027/HYP-2026-030 and the C_TTT extraction work. Precedent that holographic-tensor-network circuits are runnable and diagnostically informative on today's trapped-ion hardware (Quantinuum/IonQ class), reinforcing HYP-013/029 feasibility framing. No direct alpha=4, transport, or C_sse measurement -- HaPPY code entropy structure, not our specific force/OPE observables -- so it does not confirm or contradict those anchors, but it is a strong cross-reference for any future 'run our force/OPE circuit on real hardware' proposal.
